previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A female patient with a history of paraplegia from a gunshot wound and chronic indwelling Foley catheter use presented after a mechanical fall from her wheelchair, reporting lower back pain. Imaging of the thoracic and lumbar spine showed no definite fracture despite limited views. She was found to have a urinary tract infection caused by Escherichia coli, which was resistant to several antibiotics but sensitive to cefpodoxime. She was discharged on a 14-day course of cefpodoxime, along with tramadol, ibuprofen, acetaminophen, and a lidocaine patch for pain management. The patient was counseled on completing her antibiotic course and avoiding alcohol with tramadol. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to return if she developed fever, chills, or worsening symptoms.

TECHNIQUE:  A realtime grayscale ultrasound of the kidneys and urinary bladder
with color Doppler was performed.  Correlation is made to a prior CT scan of
the abdomen and pelvis dated ___ as well as a prior renal
ultrasound dated ___.

FINDINGS:  The kidneys are normal in contour and echotexture without focal
abnormality to suggest an abscess.  The right kidney measures 11.5 cm.  The
left kidney measures 10.4 cm.  No evidence of hydronephrosis or renal stones.
The bladder is decompressed around a Foley catheter.

IMPRESSION:  No focal renal parenchymal abnormality to suggest an abscess.  No
evidence of hydronephrosis or renal stones.
